name: Giacomo Gastaldi, La Nuova Francia, woodcut for Ramusio's Navigationi et viaggi, vol. III, Venice 1556
holding: McGill University Library, via the Internet Archive
note: The PDF wraps a single 4026x3228 JPEG; `pdfimages -j` extracts it untouched. Isola de Demoni is the large island north of Terra Nova, about 600 x 870 px, with two demons standing on its north shore, more flying above it, a hut, a tree, two birds and an archer. It is the story's plate. Chosen by Etienne in October 2026 over Ortelius' Americae sive novi orbis (1570; the 1572 impression, 12444x8980), which follows Mercator 1569 and draws 'des demonios' as one blank islet of ~45 x 55 px with two specks beside it, and over Ruysch 1507, the first appearance, two lens-shaped ovals of ~40 x 20 px set inside the legend that warns of the demons. Mercator/Ortelius is the version later maps repeated, so on the most-influential rule it was the default; but it has no shape to trace, and Ramusio's Navigationi was itself very widely read. North is up: TRAMONTANA is printed at the top of the sheet, OSTRO at the bottom.
extraction_note: --mode band. A woodcut: land and sea are the same paper, and the island's interior is drawn over as busily as the sea — a hut, a tree, birds, an archer, and long ground strokes running coast to coast — so an ink flood from inside stops in dozens of pockets (126 at threshold 110). The open sea is wave lines with paper between them, so a flood from outside walks through the coast wherever its line breaks, and probe_extraction finds no colour mode at all (best d-prime 0.1). What is continuous is the hatching cut hard against the shore: ink (grey < 110) at density > 0.25 over 15 px picks out that band and little else. The flood from inside is walled by it and grown 3 px to land on the drawn coastline. The tree against the west coast and the demons on the north shore are painted out first, since they touch the band and would otherwise come out as notches rather than holes. The north shore between x 3045 and 3245 has no band: the demons stand across it, and the coast is either drawn faintly under sparse hatching or hidden behind the horned demon's legs. It is sealed there with a polyline along the drawn shore (--seal) — a liberty, and the outline over those ~200 px is that line.
